cards.explanation: The answer is False. Luke 10:1 says the Lord sent them two by two ahead of Him. Seventy-two people, so that's thirty-six pairs heading out. Nobody had to talk to himself the whole way.

The answer is to ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers. Jesus says, “Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.” Look at what He tells them to do first, friends. He doesn't say go recruit or panic. He says ask.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.” He tells them plainly what they're walking into. I'd have asked for the whole job description twice.
The answer is a purse or bag or sandals. Jesus says, “Carry no purse or bag or sandals.” That's a short packing list, friends. Imagine the stares at the front door of the first house.

The answer is that the peace returns to them. Jesus says, “If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.” So the peace isn't tossed out the window. It comes back to the ones who said it.

The answer is True. In Luke 10:7 Jesus says, “Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered.” Then He adds, “Do not move around from house to house.” So where they're welcomed is where they settle in, friends. No house-hopping.

The answer is to heal the sick and tell them God's kingdom is near. Jesus says, “Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’” One thing to do and one thing to say, both in the same verse, bakers. They eat what's set before them, and then they bring healing and good news to the table.

The answer is the dust of the town clinging to their feet. Jesus says, “Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you.” It's a message you can see, down to the dust on their feet. And right after that comes the line, “Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.”

The word is repented. Jesus says Tyre and Sidon “…would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.” He says those two coastal cities would have done it. Chorazin and Bethsaida had the miracles performed in them, so His words to them are heavy.

The answer is that Capernaum will be brought down to Hades. Jesus says, “And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!” He asks the question and then answers it Himself. It's a heavy word for a town, friends, so I'll just say it plainly and let it sit.

The answer is the One who sent Him. Jesus says, “Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.” It's a chain with three links, bakers. The seventy-two carry His message, so how people treat them lines up with how they treat Him.

The answer is that even the demons submit to them in His name. When the seventy-two get back, they say, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.” Notice the last part, friends, in His name. They come back with a report and they point to who it's about.
The answer is False. The text says, “The seventy-two returned with joy…” That's how they walk back in, friends. Jesus then answers what they report, so you can tell they were bursting with it.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.” That's a big gift, bakers, and it comes from Him. They're not carrying it on their own.

The answer is that their names are written in heaven. Jesus says, “…do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” The demons submitting was big news, friends, and He still points them to something bigger. Their names are written in heaven.

The answer is little children. Jesus says, “…You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.” He says it while rejoicing in the Holy Spirit, bakers. And He adds, “Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.”

The answer is those the Son chooses to reveal Him to. Jesus says, “…no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.” So knowing the Father comes through the Son, friends. It's something He gives.

The answer is many prophets and kings. Jesus tells the disciples, “…many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.” That's a lot of important people who wanted what the disciples had, bakers.
